title: Issued USGS aftershock forecasts for 252 earthquakes (2024-2026) were almost calibrated after updates, but first forecasts gave 1.8 times too many events, mainly for mainshocks deeper than 70 km
abstract: Question: are the aftershock forecasts that the USGS actually issued calibrated? Approach: we downloaded all 14,249 versions of the ComCat operational aftershock forecast (oaf) products for all 252 mainshocks in ComCat, most from November 2024 to November 2026. We compared each issued probability of at least one event (M3 to M7, windows of 1 day to 1 year) with the events that ComCat later recorded in the same circle. We wrote and committed the plan before we downloaded the outcomes. We scored only bins at or above the forecast completeness magnitude, and only versions issued before their window started (368 ETAS versions for international events failed this rule). Results: the first forecast for each mainshock, mostly generic Reasenberg-Jones, expected 313.7 windows with events and 179 occurred (O/E 0.57, 95% bootstrap interval 0.44-0.71; M4+ 0.51, M5+ 0.49). Over all versions, with equal weight per mainshock, O/E was 0.89 (0.76-1.02), and windows that started after day 7 had 1.04 (0.88-1.24). The probability of an event at or above the mainshock magnitude within 1 month summed to 12.5, and 3 occurred (p = 0.002). A leave-one-mainshock-out odds multiplier of 0.38 decreased the first-forecast Brier score from 0.0411 to 0.0357. Exploratory: the 31 mainshocks deeper than 70 km (Alaska, Aleutians, Mariana Islands) received shallow generic a-values; they had 1 window with events against 35.7 expected (O/E 0.03), and updates corrected this slowly. ComCat data for 2000-2023 already showed this (11 of 134.7; a-value shift -1.91, 95% CI -2.30 to -1.62). Applied to the 2024-2026 issued forecasts for 28 deep mainshocks, this shift changed the expected count from 34.3 to 1.5 against 1 observed and decreased the Brier score from 0.0377 to 0.0030. Shallow first forecasts had O/E 0.64 (0.50-0.79), and 0.80 for shallow M6+. With a 1.5 times larger counting circle, O/E became 0.74 (first) and 1.15 (all versions), so part of the remaining deficit depends on the 10 km circle. Limitations: short period, nested bins, ComCat is both input and outcome, our counting rule may differ from the USGS rule, and the depth test has only 1 observed event and was not planned.
